thread:
sam: Heads up — payments deploy started failing after the CI service-account rotation. Builds pass but artifact upload errors out with 403. Anyone seen this pattern? :grimacing:

jon: 403 on upload — can you paste the error & minimal repro?

sam: Error log from runner: 
```
Uploading artifact to gs://redwood-artifacts/payments/1234.tgz
ERROR: 403 AccessDenied: The caller does not have permission to perform storage.objects.create on the bucket.
Request ID: abc123
```

sam: Repro steps: create new service account, grant roles used in our rotation script, update pipeline secret, trigger CI. Fail on upload.

maria: Quick audit: the rotated SA has these bindings: `roles/logging.writer`, `roles/monitoring.metricWriter`, and `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` (project-level). It is missing any Storage role. :eyes:

kate: Wait — our least-privilege checklist usually grants `roles/storage.objectCreator` on the artifacts bucket, plus `roles/storage.objectViewer` for reads. Did the rotation script skip the bucket-level binding?

sam: Looks like the script adds project-level roles only. I can repro locally with `gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=sa.json` then `gsutil cp foo.tgz gs://redwood-artifacts/payments/` which yields the same 403.

jon: Thanks. Two paths: short-term — add `roles/storage.objectCreator` scoped to the artifacts bucket to restore deploys. Long-term — update rotation infra to apply the bucket-level binding and validate via the post-rotation smoke test.

maria: Also flag: granting `storage.admin` or project Owner would be overprivileged. Keep to bucket-level `roles/storage.objectCreator` + `roles/storage.objectViewer` (for readback). Documented in our CI least-privilege matrix.

sam: Patch suggestion: run `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:payments-ci@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/storage.objectCreator --condition=None` — but we should scope to the bucket using `gsutil iam ch serviceAccount:...:objectCreator gs://redwood-artifacts`

infra-bot: deploy-canary triggered for payments with amended IAM binding. CI smoke: artifact upload step will run in ~2 min.

support-bot: Note added to incident log: INC-2026 — CI deploy blocked by rotated SA missing storage binding. Owner: sam.

kate: For the rotation script change: add a validation step that runs `gsutil -q -m cp` small artifact to the bucket using generated credentials. If it fails, rollback the SA change and notify on-call.

jon: Also add an audit rule: alert when a rotated SA has no storage bindings but is listed in the `ci-deployers` group. That would catch this earlier.

sam: I'll apply temporary bucket binding and run canary. Then update rotation code and add smoke test.

maria: After fix, let's run a 10-canary deploys run to ensure no intermittent permission edge-case (we saw earlier TTL races).

kate: Assign follow-ups: sam -> remediate & canary (ETA 20m), jon -> update rotation script PR (ETA today), maria -> add alert to infra-monitoring (ETA EOD).

sam: Done — bucket binding applied, canary succeeded (3/3). Rolling out full deploy now. :thumbsup:

jon: Thanks. Add an entry to the runbook: "CI rotation: ensure bucket-level storage.objectCreator binding or smoke test will fail the rotation."

maria: Closing note: prefer using Workload Identity or short-lived impersonation (less key leakage risk) for future rotation flows, not long-lived JSON keys.

sam: Agree — follow-up issue to migrate is created: #infra/ci-rotate-impersonation.

kate: Marking this resolved unless any downstream customer reports. :white_check_mark:
